name: Hotel Alfonso XIII
insider_take: A palatial Mudéjar masterpiece where royalty once slept and flamenco passion echoes through marble halls.
whats_special: Built in 1929 for the Ibero-American Exposition, this neo-Mudéjar palace was designed as a royal residence for King Alfonso XIII. The stunning central patio features hand-painted tiles from Triana, Seville's famous ceramic district, while the hotel's Bar Americano has been serving celebrities and dignitaries for nearly a century.
pro_tip: Request a room overlooking the central courtyard to wake up to the sound of fountains and singing birds – it's like having your own private Andalusian palace experience.
dont_miss: The hotel sits just steps from the UNESCO World Heritage trio: the Gothic Cathedral with Columbus's tomb, the Moorish Alcázar palace with its Game of Thrones filming locations, and the historic Archive of the Indies. The legendary Santa Cruz quarter's narrow streets and hidden plazas begin right at your doorstep.
pros: Historic palatial architecture with Mudéjar-style design and royal heritage
Prime location in the heart of Seville near major attractions
Exceptional personalized service with attention to detail
Beautiful courtyards and elegant interiors with authentic Spanish décor
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects exclusive positioning
Historic building may have room size variations
